catalog_quote: Las palabras en el NAHTLAX se acentúan en la penúltima sílaba y sólo ocurre un acento primario en palabras bisilábicas y trisilábicas. La cantidad vocálica no influye en la asignación del acento, como se muestra en los ejemplos en (229). (229) a. [ˈte.peːtɬ] ‗cerro‘ b. [siː.ˈtɬa.li] ‗estrella‘ c. [toː.ˈma.wakh] ‗gordo‘ d. [ˈʝo.loːtɬ] ‗corazón‘ [...] En un número reducido de palabras, el acento cae en la última sílaba. Éstas inician con la vocal [i] seguida de la fricativa glotal sorda [h] o de la nasal alveolar [n]. (230) a. [iːh.ˈkiːn ‗así (cercano)‘ b. [iːh.ˈkoːn ‗así (lejano)‘ c. [iː.ˈniːn ‗este/éste, esta/ésta, esto‘ d. [iː.ˈnoːn ‗ese/ése, esa/ésa, eso‘ [...] En el NAHTLAX, hay tres morfemas que no cuentan en la asignación del acento: -tli, -ki y -tin. En raíces bisilábicas o trisilábicas, el morfema absolutivo -tli no cuenta en la asignación del acento, es decir, el acento se asigna a la penúltima sílaba de la raíz sin contar el morfema absolutivo, como se observa en (231). (231) a. [ˈtɬa.neˑʃ<tɬ > ‗luz‘ b. [teːˈna.las<tɬ > ‗caracol‘ [...] En resumen, se concluye que el tipo de pie en el NAHTLAX es trocaico silábico, puesto que es insensible al peso y casi siempre recae en la penúltima sílaba. Hasta ahora sólo he revisado palabras bisilábicas y trisilábicas, en donde se asigna únicamente un acento primario.

new_statements.quote: En esta sección, describo la regla de acentuación y el tipo de acento en el NAHTLAX. Las palabras en el NAHTLAX se acentúan en la penúltima sílaba y sólo ocurre un acento primario en palabras bisilábicas y trisilábicas. La cantidad vocálica no influye en la asignación del acento, como se muestra en los ejemplos en (229). (229) a. [ˈte.peːtɬ] 'cerro' b. [siː.ˈtɬa.li] 'estrella' c. [toː.ˈma.wakh] 'gordo' d. [ˈʝo.loːtɬ] 'corazón' [...] En resumen, se concluye que el tipo de pie en el NAHTLAX es trocaico silábico, puesto que es insensible al peso y casi siempre recae en la penúltima sílaba.
new_statements.translation: In this section I describe the stress-assignment rule and the type of stress in NAHTLAX [the Nahuatl of Tlaxcala]. Words in NAHTLAX are stressed on the penultimate syllable, and only one primary stress occurs in disyllabic and trisyllabic words. Vowel length does not influence stress assignment, as the examples in (229) show. (229) a. [ˈte.peːtɬ] 'hill' b. [siː.ˈtɬa.li] 'star' c. [toː.ˈma.wakh] 'fat' d. [ˈʝo.loːtɬ] 'heart' [...] In sum, it is concluded that the foot type in NAHTLAX is the syllabic trochee, since it is insensitive to weight and almost always falls on the penultimate syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word regardless of vowel length (syllabic trochee; the phonetic cue is intensity, sometimes with pitch, not duration). Three suffixes are extrametrical and do not count for stress placement: the absolutive -tli ([ˈtɬa.neʃ<tɬ>] 'luz', [teːˈna.las<tɬ>] 'caracol'), the agentive nominalizer -ki ([teː.ˈpaːh.tih<ki>] 'curandero') and the plural -tin on Spanish loans ([ˈka.mion<tin>] 'camiones'), so stress falls on the penult of the stem preceding them.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described: the author states she has examined only di- and trisyllabic words, in which a single primary stress is assigned (p. 631).
new_statements.exceptions: A small set of words beginning with [i] followed by [h] or [n] carry final stress: [iːh.ˈkiːn] 'así (cercano)', [iːh.ˈkoːn] 'así (lejano)', [iː.ˈniːn] 'este', [iː.ˈnoːn] 'ese' (p. 629); extrametrical -tli, -ki, -tin (pp. 629-630).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in isolated (citation) forms, illustrated with spectrograms of single words; the variety is the Nahuatl of San Isidro Buensuceso, San Pablo del Monte, Tlaxcala (Malinche slopes). Consistent with González Casanova 1922: 606 for the Teotihuacán Valley dialect ('es más marcado el acento normal sobre la penúltima sílaba, variando algunas veces de lugar por la aposición de prefijos o sufijos con acento propio').
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Nahuatl of San Isidro Buensuceso (municipio San Pablo del Monte, Tlaxcala, on the Malinche), which the author calls NAHTLAX 'náhuatl de Tlaxcala'; Glottolog files it under cent2132 [nhn], a broad code that also covers the Texcoco/Teotihuacán (State of Mexico) and Puebla (Canoa) varieties. The corroborating 1922 remark by González Casanova is for the Teotihuacán Valley dialect (Atlatongo etc.), which Glottolog only 'probably' assigns to nhn.

new_statements.quote: El acento normalmente va en la penúúltima [sic] sílaba como en clásico y en la gran mayoría de los dialectos modernos. Pero se ha encontrado un fenómeno interesante que está relacionado con la acentuación. En algunos lugares de habla náhuatl el acento recae en la antepenúltima sílaba en sustantivos trisilábicos terminados con ciertos sufijos. [...] Los Hill (comunicación personal) comentan que en San Miguel Canoa, Pue. y en varios pueblos de las faldas de la Malinche sucede algo semejante con los sustantivos en -λi (absolutivo), -tin (plural) y -ki (agentivo). La vocal /i/ no cuenta al ponerse el acento en la antepenúltima, p. ej.: kámakλi 'boca', nákastin 'orejas', tepáhtiki 'curandero', pero esto no sucede así si en la palabra se da -cin (rev.) o -ton (dim.): mecínλi 'luna' (rev.).
new_statements.translation: Stress normally goes on the penultimate syllable, as in Classical Nahuatl and in the great majority of the modern dialects. But an interesting phenomenon related to accentuation has been found. In some Nahuatl-speaking places stress falls on the antepenultimate syllable in trisyllabic nouns ending in certain suffixes. [...] The Hills (personal communication) remark that in San Miguel Canoa, Puebla, and in several villages on the slopes of La Malinche something similar happens with nouns in -λi (absolutive), -tin (plural) and -ki (agentive). The vowel /i/ does not count when stress is placed on the antepenult, e.g. kámakλi 'mouth', nákastin 'ears', tepáhtiki 'healer', but this does not happen if the word contains -cin (reverential) or -ton (diminutive): mecínλi 'moon' (rev.).

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog (penultimate, Flores Nájera 2019 for San Isidro Buensuceso): 'El acento normalmente va en la penúltima sílaba'. Adds a morphologically conditioned deviation reported for the very area of the catalog variety (Malinche slopes, San Miguel Canoa): absolutive -λi, plural -tin, agentive -ki do not count for stress, giving antepenultimate surface stress (kámakλi, nákastin, tepáhtiki). Flores Nájera's sketch instead gives penultimate [siː.ˈtɬa.li] and lists only a small set of finally-stressed words; her sketch does not mention an antepenultimate pattern, so the 1979 report (second-hand, Hill & Hill p.c.) is a refinement to check against Hill & Hill 1986, not a differe…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Tlaxcala Nahuatl stress is normally penultimate, as in Classical and most modern dialects. Reported deviation (Hill & Hill p.c.) for San Miguel Canoa and several Malinche-slope villages: the /i/ of absolutive -λi, plural -tin and agentive -ki is not counted, so such trisyllabic nouns surface with antepenultimate stress (kámakλi, nákastin, tepáhtiki), unless reverential -cin or diminutive -ton is present (mecínλi). In Tlaxcala proper the authors found that nouns with a disyllabic root and Classical absolutive -λi/-li (except at Ixtacuixtla) end in a consonant with no final /i/ (tónal 'sol', λáškal 'tortilla', kóyok 'agujero'), which they derive historically from a stage with fixed penultimate stress (pp. 301-302).
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenultimate surface stress on trisyllabic nouns in -λi, -tin, -ki in San Miguel Canoa and Malinche-slope villages (suffix vowel /i/ not counted), blocked by -cin (rev.) and -ton (dim.); San Bernardino Teotitlan (Oaxaca) and Zacapoaxtla comparanda; Tequixquitla patterns with the Sierra de Puebla (ta:l).
new_statements.identity_note: Catalog record = NAHTLAX of San Isidro Buensuceso, San Pablo del Monte, Tlaxcala (Malinche slopes). Lastra & Horcasitas 1979 = dialect survey of Nahuatl across the state of Tlaxcala (74 communities, fieldwork 1978; vocabularies of San Pedro Tlalcuapan and Tequixquitla; San Pablo del Monte vocabulary supplied by the Hills), i.e. the same variety cluster. Foster 1969 = philological reconstruction of Tetzcoco Nahuatl of A.D. 1520 from colonial grammars (Classical Nahuatl, Glottolog clas1250), filed under cent2132 by Glottolog but not a description of the modern Tlaxcala language.

readall_conflicts: No disagreement on the basic rule: the catalog (Flores Nájera 2019, San Isidro Buensuceso) and Lastra & Horcasitas 1979 (74 Tlaxcala communities) both give penultimate stress, and Foster 1969 gives penultimate stress for reconstructed 16th-century Tetzcoco (Classical) Nahuatl with final stress only in vocatives. One point to keep in view rather than a contradiction: Lastra & Horcasitas (p. 300) relay Hill & Hill's personal communication that in San Miguel Canoa and several Malinche-slope villages trisyllabic nouns in absolutive -λi, plural -tin and agentive -ki carry antepenultimate surface stress because the suffix /i/ is not counted (kámakλi, nákastin, tepáhtiki; not with -cin/-ton), whereas Flores Nájera's sketch for a Malinche-slope town states plain penultimate stress (e.g. [siː.ˈtɬa.li]) and mentions only a small set of finally-stressed words; this second-hand 1979 report should be checked against Hill & Hill 1986 (Speaking Mexicano), still unread.
